deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 11-13): Grothendieck is building a category E = E_mod (or E_{M_n}) of 'tame' (modéré) spaces. It is generated by systems M_n of tame subsets of R^n, subject to axioms M1, M2, ... A map is tame if its graph is a tame subset (previous page). The previous page proves two things. First, tame maps glue along inductive systems. Second, for a tame map f: X -> Y, the quotient X/R_f exists in E and is canonically f(X).

This page adds two axioms.
(M6) For tame Z ⊂ X there is a finite family of tame functions f_α: X -> R and 'rational' constants e_α ∈ R_0 (presumably the distinguished, definable constants) such that Z = ∩ f_α^{-1}(e_α). One may moreover assume the f_α separate the points of X \ Z.
- Write F = (f_α): X -> R^A. Then F is constant equal to e on Z, injective on X \ Z, and F(X \ Z) avoids e.
- So the equivalence relation R_F collapses exactly Z. By the previous corollary, X/Z exists and equals F(X) ⊂ R^A.
- Hence the contraction X/Z exists in E 'au sens strict', i.e. it commutes with the underlying-set functor X ↦ |X|.
- The crossed-out diagram records the equivalent embedded picture. Take x ↦ (x, F(x)), giving X ↪ R^n × R^A, with Z the preimage of R^n × {e}.
(M7) Tame functions Z -> R extend to tame functions X -> R (a tame Tietze/extension axiom).

Proposition: given M5, M6, M7, amalgamated sums X1 ⊔_Z X2 along tame embeddings exist in E_{M_n} and commute with the forgetful functors.

The proof is on the next page:
1. Embed Z ⊂ R^I and extend the embedding to g_i: X_i -> R^I by M7.
2. By M6 choose F_i: X_i -> R^{A_i} collapsing exactly Z_i to e_i and injective elsewhere.
3. Then (g_i, F_i) embeds X_i with Z = X_i ∩ (R^I × {e_i}).
4. Place X1 in R^I × R^{A1} × {e2} and X2 in R^I × {e1} × R^{A2}. These two affine pieces meet in R^I × {e1} × {e2}, and each X_i meets it exactly in Z.
5. The union X1 ∪ X2 ⊂ R^{I ⊔ A1 ⊔ A2} is therefore the set-theoretic pushout.
6. A map out of it is tame iff its restrictions are, since its graph is a union of two tame graphs.

Purpose: to show the tame category has the finite colimits needed for gluing (quotients by a subspace, pushouts along embeddings), computed on underlying sets. This is a step toward a tame 'dévissage' category of stratified spaces.
errors: Interpretation dependence. If 'modérée' means only 'tame graph' (as on the previous page), maps need not be continuous. Then M6 and M7 are nearly trivial in any o-minimal-type setting: use indicator functions 1_{X\Z}, x_i·1_{X\Z}, and extension by 0. The proposition is then essentially a set-level (definable) statement.

If continuity is intended, M6 forces Z to be closed in X and is a Łojasiewicz-type zero-set statement. In that case the image F(X) ⊂ R^A generally does NOT carry the topological quotient topology when Z is closed but non-compact. Example: collapsing a line in R^2 gives a non-first-countable topological quotient, while F(X) is metrizable. So 'au sens strict' can only mean commuting with underlying sets, not with the topological quotient. The page does not address this.
The proof that X/Z ≅ F(X) tacitly needs F(X) to be tame, i.e. that images of tame maps are tame (presumably one of M1-M5). It also needs e ∈ R_0 so that {e} is a tame point.
Minor: the injectivity of (g_i, F_i) and the identity Z = X_i ∩ (R^I × {e_i}) both use F_i^{-1}(e_i) = Z. This is fine but is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Axiom M6: every tame subset is a fibre of a finite tame map that is injective off the subset, so that contractions X/Z exist and commute with the underlying-set functor
ideas.modern_name: Definable zero sets (Łojasiewicz-type) / existence of definable quotients, a special case of elimination of imaginaries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Łojasiewicz (semialgebraic zero sets); van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures (1998), ch. 6 and ch. 10 (definable quotients); Pillay; Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic quotients)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 only sketches tame topology programmatically; no such axioms

ideas.what: Axiom M7: tame functions on a tame subset extend to the ambient tame set
Existence of pushouts X1 ⊔_Z X2 along tame embeddings, realized concretely inside R^I × R^{A1} × R^{A2}, commuting with forgetful functors
ideas.modern_name: Definable gluing / pushouts of definable sets (definable spaces); finite colimits in the category of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries 1998 (gluing of definable spaces); Delfs–Knebusch for semialgebraic/locally semialgebraic spaces (1980s)

ideas.what: Axiomatic approach: a family M_n of tame subsets of R^n with closure axioms, from which categorical properties (quotients, amalgamations) of E_{M_n} are derived
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal structure / the category Def of definable sets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the need for axiomatizing 'tame' structures, without axioms

missed.claim: Grothendieck frames the key question as whether quotients (here X/Z, and on the previous page X/R_f) exist in the tame category 'au sens strict', commuting with the underlying-set functor. He isolates sufficient axioms (M6, M7) for finite colimits along embeddings. This is precisely the categorical form of elimination of imaginaries: whether the category of definable sets is already effective, i.e. a pretopos à la Makkai–Reyes. Model theorists derived this for o-minimal expansions of fields only later, and the link to Grothendieck's tame-topology programme is not made in the literature.
missed.quote: ce qui signifie en fait que le quotient X/Z (contraction de Z en un seul point) existe dans E au sens strict (i.e. X ↦ |X| y commute)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's tame topology was aimed at a category with good quotients and gluings computed on points. This is the property later central to o-minimal homotopy theory and to definable/tame stacks. It is relevant to historical claims that the Esquisse 'anticipated' o-minimality.

missed.claim: The left-margin notes suggest a generalization of the amalgamation result under weaker conditions (quotients X -> Z, a construction X^~). These remain unworked here.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The general statement is now covered by o-minimal definable-gluing theory.

deep.surprise_reason: An early axiomatic, categorical treatment of tame quotients and pushouts, predating o-minimality. Historically interesting as evidence of how concrete Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics were. The mathematics itself (definable quotients, Tietze extension, gluing) was later established independently and is standard.

The crossed-out line reads roughly 'indiquons que ceci peut se traduire par un diagramme', not 'les peut traiter'.

'existe dans E au sens strict': E is probably E_{M_n} or E_mod.
